8. Decisive smaller physical experiment

The most informative next physical test is an integrated loaded pod, independent escape and restoration test, with a matched assisted control. A free-standing latch coupon would miss the main ambiguities.

The proposed campaign has 80 attempts: 40 automated and 40 competent assisted, randomized over the same hardware and information. It includes both joint-coupon families and repeated retrieval and reset.

The loaded extension uses approximately 225 kg of weighed ballast, giving about 2.21 kN before fixture contributions. Its actual inertia, guide friction and force path must be measured. A source-only check must show that the guide is not secretly supporting the tested load.

Challenges include:

An internal guide seizure that fools a rear sensor but should not fool the front channel.
Full-depth apparent seating with missing positive engagement.
Dirty and worn contact datums.
Persistent and partly open support jams.
A seized final foot.
A seized robot coupling while carrying the pod.
A jam combined with one-hour power loss.
Complete recovery, cleaning, comparison, spare installation and final clearance.

An independent party inserts the fault. Neither the controller nor the assisted operator receives its label.

Measurements include front and rear forces, keeper reactions, workpiece pose, internal travel, screw angle, lock position, gas state, temperatures, full-meter energy, all stock changes and human time. Independent observations must verify that every temporary path is gone at the endpoint.
